column2: Horse. A big, fast animal that neighs. A horse has strong legs and hard hooves. It loves to eat hay, oats and apples.
A big, fast animal that neighs.
Horse
Sheep. A farm animal with soft wool that says baa. Sheep wool is used to make warm sweaters and socks. Sheep live together in a flock.
A farm animal with soft wool that says baa.
Sheep
Pig. A pink farm animal with a snout that says oink. A pig digs in the ground with its snout to find food. When it is hot, it rolls in mud to cool down.
A pink farm animal with a snout that says oink.
Pig
Duck. A bird that swims and says quack-quack. A duck has webbed feet, so it swims very well. Its feathers stay dry in the water.
A bird that swims and says quack-quack.
Duck
Frog. A small green animal that jumps and croaks. A frog lives both in water and on land. It catches flies with its long, sticky tongue.
A small green animal that jumps and croaks.
Frog
Rooster. A farm bird that crows cock-a-doodle-doo in the morning. A rooster crows early in the morning and wakes people up. It lives in a henhouse with the hens.
A farm bird that crows cock-a-doodle-doo in the morning.
Rooster
Thunder. A loud rumble in the sky during a storm. We see the lightning first and hear the thunder later, because light travels faster than sound.
A loud rumble in the sky during a storm.
Thunder
Snow. Soft white flakes that fall in winter. Snow is frozen water. Every snowflake has six points and is different from all the others.
Soft white flakes that fall in winter.
Snow
Flower. A colorful part of a plant that smells nice. Bees fly from flower to flower to collect nectar for honey. Later, fruits grow from flowers.
A colorful part of a plant that smells nice.
Flower
Sea. A big body of salty water with splashing waves. Fish, crabs and dolphins live in the sea. Seas and oceans cover most of the Earth.
A big body of salty water with splashing waves.
Sea
Remember: Swim only with an adult and only where there is a lifeguard.
Door. We open and close it to go into a house or a room. A door can creak when it opens. Before you enter someone else's room, knock first.
We open and close it to go into a house or a room.
Door
Remember: Do not open the door to strangers. Call an adult first.
Key. A small metal object that unlocks a door. Every key has its own special teeth and opens only its own lock.
A small metal object that unlocks a door.
Key
Remember: Keep your house key in a safe place and do not show it to strangers.
Scissors. A tool with two sharp blades for cutting paper. Scissors cut when their two blades slide past each other. There are also children's scissors with rounded tips.
A tool with two sharp blades for cutting paper.
Scissors
Remember: Carry scissors with the points facing down and use them only with an adult.
Toothbrush. We use it with toothpaste every morning and evening to clean our mouth. Brush your teeth twice a day, in the morning and in the evening, for two minutes. This keeps your teeth healthy.
We use it with toothpaste every morning and evening to clean our mouth.
Toothbrush
Glass. A cup we drink water or milk from. A glass can be made of glass or plastic. Hold a glass cup carefully so it does not break.
A cup we drink water or milk from.
Glass
Earth. The blue planet we live on. The Earth goes around the Sun once every year. It is the only planet we know that has life.
The blue planet we live on.
Earth
Astronaut. A person who travels into space in a special suit. An astronaut wears a spacesuit with air to breathe. In space, astronauts float like feathers.
A person who travels into space in a special suit.
Astronaut
Comet. An icy space object with a long bright tail. A comet is made of ice, dust and rock. When it comes close to the Sun, it grows a bright tail.
An icy space object with a long bright tail.
Comet
Satellite. A machine that circles the Earth and sends signals. Satellites help us watch TV, check the weather forecast and find our way.
A machine that circles the Earth and sends signals.
Satellite
UFO. A flying saucer from stories about aliens. These letters stand for unidentified flying object. In stories and cartoons, aliens travel in it.
A flying saucer from stories about aliens.
UFO
Telescope. A tool for looking at faraway stars and planets. A telescope makes faraway things look close. Scientists use it to explore space.
A tool for looking at faraway stars and planets.
Telescope
Piano. A big musical instrument with black and white keys. When you press a key, a small hammer hits a string and makes a note. A piano has 88 keys.
A big musical instrument with black and white keys.
Piano
Violin. A small wooden instrument with strings, played with a bow. A violin is held under the chin. When the bow slides across the strings, it sings softly.
A small wooden instrument with strings, played with a bow.
Violin
Trumpet. A shiny metal instrument you blow into loudly. The player buzzes their lips while blowing and changes the notes with three buttons.
A shiny metal instrument you blow into loudly.
Trumpet
Saxophone. A curved golden instrument you blow into, loved in jazz music. The saxophone was invented by Adolphe Sax. It is made of metal, but a small piece of reed makes its sound.
A curved golden instrument you blow into, loved in jazz music.
Saxophone
Accordion. An instrument with keys and bellows that squeeze and stretch. An accordion plays when its bellows pull in and push out air. It is often played at weddings and folk celebrations.
An instrument with keys and bellows that squeeze and stretch.
Accordion
Banjo. A string instrument with a round body like a little drum. A banjo has a bright, cheerful sound. It is most often played in American country music.
A string instrument with a round body like a little drum.
Banjo
Microphone. A device we sing or talk into so we can be heard louder. A microphone catches our voice and sends it to the speakers. Singers use it at concerts.
A device we sing or talk into so we can be heard louder.
Microphone
